short: Sweden officially entered the Thirty Years' War by allying with the Duchy of Pomerania.
full:
On 4 September 1630, Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden and Bogislaw XIV, Duke of Pomerania, signed the Treaty of Stettin. The agreement followed the Swedish landing at Usedom a few months earlier, providing a vital bridgehead and logistical base for Swedish operations in northern Germany.

The treaty granted Sweden full military control over Pomerania, which was nominally allied but effectively occupied. This formalized Sweden's entry into the broader German conflict, securing their supply lines across the Baltic and laying the foundation for their subsequent campaigns deep into the Holy Roman Empire.
